title: Routine structural reading of complex glycans

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a practical, reliable workflow for identifying and quantifying complex glycans in small biological samples. Reading a glycan means determining more than its constituent sugars: it requires distinguishing how those sugars are connected, where branches occur, the configurations of linkages, and relevant chemical modifications. Closely related structures can differ in these features, so reporting composition alone would not meet the goal.

Glycans are assembled through enzymatic biosynthesis rather than copied directly from a simple genetic template. Their structural diversity therefore cannot be read directly from a corresponding genetic sequence. Existing analytical methods provide valuable information, but characterization can demand substantial expertise, sufficient sample and complementary measurements. The innovation would make detailed structural analysis routine across a declared, broad range of glycans; it need not take the form of a single instrument or characterize every possible glycan.

significance.text: If achieved with broad coverage, reliable quantification and practical throughput, routine glycan reading would be a major enabling capability for biochemistry. It would open an important class of biomolecules to systematic comparisons across biological samples at a scale now constrained by analytical effort and sample requirements. More accessible measurements would directly expand comparative glycomics and help researchers connect specific structural differences with biological observations.

The scientific value extends beyond cataloguing structures. Glycans participate in molecular recognition, and differences in linkage, branching or modifications such as sulfation can matter for binding and function. Better structural measurements would provide more precise inputs for experiments testing those relationships. Defined synthetic glycans could complement these measurements as standards and experimental probes, helping investigators test the consequences of particular structural features.

The analogy to routine sequencing is useful as a description of accessibility and scale, but it has limits. Glycan structures include branching, linkage configurations and modifications, and they are not direct copies of a genetic template. Structural identification would also remain distinct from explaining biological mechanisms: functional conclusions would require perturbations, binding assays and appropriate biological presentation. Diagnostic or therapeutic applications are conditional downstream possibilities requiring separate validation; successful structural reading alone would not establish clinical usefulness.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is broad, dependable structural identification and quantification in complex biological samples with manageable sample input and operator effort. The central scientific difficulty is distinguishing structurally similar glycans that differ in connectivity, branching, linkage configuration or modifications. A useful workflow must resolve those distinctions within its stated scope, rather than assigning a detailed structure where the measurements support only composition or an unresolved set of alternatives.

The engineering challenge includes obtaining enough discriminating information from limited material and making its interpretation reproducible without exceptional specialist intervention. Mass spectrometry, liquid chromatography and nuclear magnetic resonance offer different kinds of structural information. Their complementary use can help characterization, but the supplied evidence does not establish that every glycan analysis must combine all three. The goal is a reliable overall workflow, with clear limits on what its measurements can distinguish.

Reference materials are an enabling challenge. Automated synthesis can produce defined glycans for standards and biological experiments, but complex preparation, deprotection and purification remain demanding, and laborious synthesis and purification can introduce reproducibility problems. Better synthesis would strengthen validation and functional follow-up, but producing a known glycan does not itself solve the analytical task of reading unknown biological mixtures.

Engineering synthesis: a convincing implementation would also need to connect structural assignments with quantitative estimates, uncertainty and explicit missingness. It must distinguish an absent glycan from one that was not detected or could not be resolved. Integrating these outputs with practical cost and throughput is part of the proposed breakthrough, rather than an established capability demonstrated by the supplied sources.

current_state.text: The review published on 15 May 2024, “In silico simulation of glycosylation and related pathways,” identifies mass spectrometry, liquid chromatography and nuclear magnetic resonance as existing glycan characterization methods. It describes their requirements for technical expertise and sufficient sample, and reports that no sequencer technology then fully characterized glycans. This is a dated assessment of an analytical limitation, not a claim that existing methods provide no useful structural information.

The review published on 12 February 2025, “Expediting Glycospace Exploration: Therapeutic Glycans via Automated Synthesis,” describes advances in automated production of defined glycans, including biological standards and targets relevant to therapeutic research. Its examples include branched glycans, linkage configuration reassignment and sulfation patterns, illustrating why detailed structural distinctions matter. It also identifies continuing synthesis, deprotection and purification challenges. These achievements concern making specified structures and supporting their study; they do not demonstrate a broadly applicable workflow for reading unknown glycan mixtures.

The supplied evidence establishes these capabilities and limitations at the reviews’ publication dates. It does not determine whether a generally applicable workflow meeting the proposed completion criterion was available by 1 November 2026, because the supplied freshness record contains no subsequent assessment. Continued absence at that date therefore remains an open question in this record. That evidence gap neither invalidates the historical assessments nor demonstrates that the proposed innovation has been achieved.

The supplied review reports complete, untruncated article text for both sources: a ten-page PDF text for the 2024 review and full XML text for the 2025 review. It reports verified article identities and no extraction issues, but the figures were not visually inspected. The qualitative conclusions here rely on the textual evidence described in that review; they do not depend on independent inspection of figures or underlying experimental datasets.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independent laboratories would evaluate the workflow in blinded studies using both defined standards and diverse biological samples. Before testing, the protocol would specify the intended glycan classes, relevant branching, linkage and modification distinctions, sample types and input amounts. Success would require identifying and quantifying a broad range within that declared scope, with unresolved alternatives reported explicitly.
completion_criteria.label: Blinded interlaboratory studies identify and quantify glycans within declared scope

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: defined standards would test whether closely related structures are distinguished correctly, while biological samples would test performance in realistic mixtures. Results should report structural assignment accuracy, quantitative accuracy, reproducibility, coverage, uncertainty and missingness. Where appropriate, independent characterization could help establish reference assignments. The protocol should make clear which structural details are measured directly and which remain inferred.
completion_criteria.label: Structural and quantitative performance reported with measured versus inferred details

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: sample requirements, cost, throughput and operator expertise should be specified in advance for the intended study scale, then measured during evaluation. Numerical acceptance thresholds would need to be chosen for those uses; none are established by the supplied record. Reproduction across laboratories and runs would be necessary to show that the workflow is routine rather than dependent on a single expert implementation.
completion_criteria.label: Measured resource requirements and reproducibility across laboratories and runs

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation of completion: success would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested classes, sample conditions and performance limits. Finite validation cannot establish literal universality, and complete characterization of every possible glycan is not required. Any subsequent claim about biological mechanism or clinical utility would require its own evidence beyond this analytical demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Demonstrated glycan breadth bounded by tested conditions and performance limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis — BCH-05, “Routine, comprehensive single-cell proteoform reading,” overlaps where glycans are attached to proteins and contribute to proteoform diversity. BCH-11 focuses on resolving the glycan structures themselves and also covers glycans outside proteins. Detailed glycan reading would not by itself establish comprehensive protein identification, attachment-site assignment or single-cell proteoform coverage.

Roster-based synthesis — BCH-10, “Predict modification-dependent biochemical networks,” overlaps because protein-associated glycans are modifications whose structural differences may affect biochemical interactions. BCH-11 could supply measured structures for such studies. Predicting how those modifications change network behavior is a separate capability from measuring glycan identity and abundance.

Roster-based synthesis — BCH-02, “Predict biochemical function from molecular sequence and environment,” shares an interest in connecting molecular features to function. Glycan measurements could improve the molecular information available for those predictions. BCH-11 addresses structural measurement, however, and glycan biosynthesis is not direct copying from a simple genetic template; structural reading alone does not determine function.

unresolved_issues: Whether a workflow meeting the proposed breadth, reliability and practical requirements was available by 1 November 2026 remains unassessed in the supplied freshness record.
The target glycan classes, required isomer distinctions, biological sample types and input amounts remain unspecified.
Quantitative acceptance thresholds for assignment accuracy, quantification, coverage, reproducibility, cost and throughput require an advance evaluation protocol; the supplied sources establish none.
The supplied review supports qualitative textual conclusions, but figures and underlying experimental datasets were not independently inspected.

brief.title: Routine reading of complex sugar molecules
possible: Researchers could take a small biological sample and routinely identify and measure its glycans: chains of sugars. They could determine how the sugars connect and branch, how their connections are oriented, and which chemical modifications they carry.
why: This would let biologists compare these molecules across samples with less analytical effort and material. They could connect precise structural differences with biological observations.

Glycans help molecules recognise and bind one another. Reading their structures would give researchers better starting points for experiments testing how particular branches, connections or modifications affect their function.

sources.who: Yukie Akune-Taylor, Akane Kon and Kiyoko F. Aoki-Kinoshita
sources.showed: Their review describes tools for predicting how cells build glycans. It reports that existing measurement methods need specialist skills and sufficient material, and that no sequencing technology then fully characterised glycans.
sources.quote:
All these technologies require highly technical skills 
and sufficient amounts of samples to analyze.
sources.cited_for: It explains why detailed glycan analysis remains demanding and why genetic information alone cannot reveal the structures.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate routine identification and measurement of a broad range of glycans in small biological samples.

sources.showed: Their review describes automated methods for making specified glycans, including biological reference materials. It also describes continuing difficulties in preparing and purifying them.
sources.quote: Automated solid‐phase oligosaccharide synthesis was first achieved by Seeberger and co‐workers in 2001 using a modified peptide synthesiser.
sources.cited_for: Making known glycans provides reference materials for testing structural measurements and experiments on biological function.
sources.not_established: Making a specified glycan does not establish a method for identifying unknown glycans in biological mixtures.

shown: Existing methods can reveal glycan structures, but require expertise and sufficient sample. Akune-Taylor and colleagues describe these limits; Suri and Gilmour review automated production of known structures that can serve as reference materials.
missing: A dependable workflow must distinguish closely related structures and measure their amounts across a broad, stated range of biological samples.
Results must distinguish a glycan that is absent from one that was missed or whose structure could not be resolved.
Independent laboratories must reproduce the results with practical sample needs, cost, speed and operator effort.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories identify and measure glycans in blind tests
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to identify and measure a broad, predefined range in blind tests of known materials and biological samples. This would test reliability without advance knowledge of the answers.

milestones.label: Performance distinguishes measured details from inferred structures
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to report structural and quantity accuracy, consistency, coverage, uncertainty and missed results, separating measured details from inference. This would reveal which conclusions the measurements support.

milestones.label: Practical resource needs and reproducibility are demonstrated
milestones.explanation: Evaluations would have to measure sample needs, cost, speed and expertise against preset requirements, with consistent results across laboratories and runs. This would establish whether routine use is practical.

milestones.label: Broad coverage has clearly demonstrated boundaries
milestones.explanation: Validation would have to establish coverage within tested glycan classes, sample conditions and performance limits. This would define success without requiring every possible glycan to be readable.

uncertain: Which glycan classes, structural distinctions, sample types and sample amounts should the workflow cover?
What accuracy, coverage, cost and speed would make the workflow useful for its intended studies?
Successful structural reading would leave biological mechanisms and clinical usefulness as separate questions.

page.title: Glycan sequencing
page.definition: Methods routinely determine complete structures of glycans—chains of sugars—including sugar identities and order, branch points, bond positions and orientations, and chemical modifications.

goal.need: In a NIST comparison, 76 laboratories submitted 103 reports for an antibody and an enzymatically modified counterpart; individual reports identified 4–48 glycan compositions. Consensus values covered 57 compositions, but compositions leave linkage isomers unresolved. A review published on 15 May 2024 described structural-analysis methods as requiring specialist skills and sufficient sample.

figures.caption: Coverage in the NIST antibody glycosylation comparison
figures.note: Composition specifies sugar counts; it does not establish complete molecular structure.

statements.context: The programme goal presented on 25 January 2024.

statements.quote: structure determination of carbohydrate structures and complex mixtures
statements.context: Recommendation 2 calls for prioritizing transformative tools for this task at NIH, NSF, DOE and FDA.

completion.title: Any glycan or polymer repeat unit can have its complete structure determined routinely.
completion.criterion: Routinely determine complete structures of any glycan or polymer repeat sequence, including branching, anomeric linkages and substituents.
completion.set_by: National Research Council, Transforming Glycoscience (2012), Recommendation 2 roadmap goals.
completion.threshold_quote: complete carbohydrate structure of any glycan
completion.basis: This is the roadmap’s explicit structural-analysis target. It leaves routine operation without numerical acceptance limits.

milestones.title: Two sialyllactose linkage isomers are distinguished and quantified in binary mixtures.
milestones.criterion: Distinguish 3′- and 6′-sialyllactose tagged with 1-methoxy-4-phenoxybenzene in the published binary-mixture experiment. Five mixtures contain 20%, 40%, 50%, 60% and 80% 3′-sialyllactose. Li et al., published on 28 March 2023, estimated 18.94%, 44.93%, 51.55%, 56.45% and 76.96%, respectively. The protocol tests linkage-isomer discrimination and relative quantification; it supplies no universal error tolerance.
milestones.set_by: Li et al., Nature Communications (2023), published nanopore binary-mixture protocol, Figure 2a–c; this benchmark concerns tagged sialyllactose.
milestones.threshold_quote: a pair of glycan linage isomers (6SL-MPB and 3SL-MPB) can be clearly distinguished.

milestones.title: Glycan abundance ratios achieve NIST’s target-plot comparability distance below 2.
milestones.criterion: For modified/unmodified NISTmAb glycan-abundance ratios, obtain target-plot distance d < 2, the paper’s category for good agreement with consensus. Here d = √(mean standardized bias² + bias variability²), using the paper’s robust consensus estimates. The 2020 study received 103 reports from 76 laboratories and evaluated ratios for 57 compositions reported at least six times. This benchmark assesses composition-level quantification, without requiring complete structural assignment.
milestones.set_by: NIST-coordinated interlaboratory study, published in Molecular & Cellular Proteomics (2020), target-plot analysis; the benchmark concerns antibody N-glycans.
milestones.threshold_quote: dots within two comparability units are colored green

milestones.title: Open-source software annotates an entire glycan profile with minimal user interaction.
milestones.criterion: Produce open-source software that automatically annotates an entire glycan profile with minimal user interaction. CandyCrunch, published on 1 July 2024, used a collection of 500,000 annotated tandem mass spectra and implemented prediction, automated curation and fragment annotation. Its abstract does not establish complete annotation of every glycan in a sample.
milestones.set_by: National Research Council, 2012 roadmap, informatics goal under Recommendation 4.
milestones.threshold_quote: automatically annotate an entire glycan profile

milestones.title: All N- and O-linked glycans from one cell type are sequenced within one week.
milestones.criterion: Sequence all N- and O-linked glycans from one cell type within one week. These glycans attach to proteins through nitrogen and oxygen, respectively. Xia et al., published online on 10 March 2026, reported reconstruction of the branching of one model N-glycan from fragments; that experiment does not establish this cell-wide target.
milestones.set_by: National Research Council, 2012 roadmap, Recommendation 2; this target specifically concerns N- and O-linked glycans.

results.finding: MPB-tagged sialyllactose isomers were quantified in 5 binary mixtures; the 50% 3′-isomer mixture was estimated at 51.55%.
results.detail: For mixtures containing 20%, 40%, 60% and 80% 3′-sialyllactose, the respective estimates were 18.94%, 44.93%, 56.45% and 76.96%. Aerolysin nanopore data were analyzed using an algorithm that optimized Jensen-Shannon divergence.
results.quote:
For the
equimolar mixture, the algorithm procedure reported a weight of
51.55% for 3SL-MPB (Supplementary Fig. 18), showing high accuracy.

results.finding: CandyCrunch, trained on 500,000 annotated spectra, achieved 90.3% top-1 glycan structure prediction accuracy.
results.detail: The open-source workflow automates prediction, curation and fragment annotation, but does not establish complete annotation of every glycan in a sample. Predictions include false positives and negatives; novel structures and some modifications remain challenging.
results.quote:
Trained on a newly curated set of 500,000 annotated  
MS/MS spectra, here we present CandyCrunch, a dilated residual neural 
network predicting glycan structure from raw liquid chromatography– 
MS/MS data in seconds (top-1 accuracy: 90.3%).

results.finding: A pooled sample from three human cell lines yielded complete structures for 25 cell-surface O-glycans.
results.detail: The study analyzed membrane fractions, not all glycans from a cell type. Less abundant O-glycan structures could not be elucidated, and the N-glycan structures were putative. Total sequencing time was not reported.
results.quote: This approach yielded the structures of 25 glycans representing over 85% of the total abundance
